# API Migration Guide: v1 to v2

This document describes the breaking changes introduced in API v2 and provides
step-by-step instructions for migrating your integration. We recommend completing
the migration before the v1 deprecation date of June 30, 2024.

## Authentication Changes

The most significant change in v2 is the move from API key authentication to
OAuth 2.0 with short-lived access tokens. This improves security by eliminating
long-lived credentials that can be leaked or compromised.

Previously, you would include your API key directly in the request header:

```
Authorization: Bearer sk-your-api-key-here
```

In v2, you first exchange your client credentials for an access token, then use
that token for subsequent requests. Access tokens expire after 1 hour.

## Endpoint Changes

The following table summarizes the endpoint changes between v1 and v2:

| v1 Endpoint | v2 Endpoint | Notes |
|------------|------------|-------|
| GET /users | GET /v2/users | Pagination now required |
| POST /users | POST /v2/users | Request body schema changed |
| GET /users/:id | GET /v2/users/:id | Response includes `metadata` |
| DELETE /users/:id | DELETE /v2/users/:id | Now returns 202 Accepted |
| GET /reports | GET /v2/analytics/reports | Moved under analytics |
| POST /export | POST /v2/analytics/export | Async with webhook callback |

## Rate Limiting

Rate limits have been adjusted in v2 to better reflect actual usage patterns.
The new limits are applied per-organization rather than per-API-key, which means
all team members share a common pool of requests.

| Tier | v1 Limit | v2 Limit | Burst |
|------|---------|---------|-------|
| Free | 60/min | 100/min | 20 |
| Pro | 600/min | 1000/min | 100 |
| Enterprise | 6000/min | 10000/min | 500 |

If you exceed the rate limit, the API returns a 429 status code with a
`Retry-After` header indicating how many seconds to wait before retrying.

## Error Response Format

Error responses now follow the RFC 7807 Problem Details specification. This
provides a more structured and consistent format for error information across
all endpoints.
